pages.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ gives out heat, and turns four volumes of gas into two. So $(thing)ΔG° = ΔH − TΔS$() climbs as it gets hotter and the equilibrium constant $(thing)K = e^(−ΔG°/RT)$() falls: cold and pressed makes the most ammonia. But the iron catalyst is sluggish when cold.

The $(item)Haber-Bosch Reactor$() sets the bed temperature, the pressure and the H₂ : N₂ ratio. A pass needs 15% ammonia; how much comes out follows the yield times the rate. The classic answer is about 720 K and 200 atm, 3 : 1. Above 823 K the $(item)Iron Catalyst$() sinters and wears ten times as fast; the vessel is rated to 300 atm.
